searchText: b"h robots and sitemap architecture boruch hashem. blessed is he. the awtsmoos gathers every public doorway without confusing abundance with exposure; awtsmoos.com should show google only canonical public vessels, while hidden chambers remain outside the map and the torah road stays in repose. evidence geelooy has no root awtsmoos.derech.js; root files are naturally static. there is currently no real robots.txt or sitemap implementation. /api/social/heichelos/discover already enforces persisted public visibility, discoverable !== false, and excludes debug, fixture, internal, staging, and test environments by default. heichel discovery pagination uses limit plus an opaque cursor; meta.pageinfo.nextcursor and hasmore prove continuation. series details includes both child subseries ids and posts. numeric road urls canonicalize to named series post urls and therefore must not appear in sitemaps. google supports multiple sitemap: lines in robots.txt and recommends canonical absolute urls in sitemaps. chosen architecture static root robots /robots.txt is a static root file. it allows ordinary crawling and advertises: https://awtsmoos.com/sitemap.xml https://awtsmoos.com/heichelos/sitemap.xml this avoids inventing a root dynamic router. static root core sitemap /sitemap.xml is a small root url set for canonical public entry points only, initially / and /heichelos. dynamic heichel sitemap index /heichelos/sitemap.xml is a sitemap index. it follows every page of the privacy filtered public discovery api and emits one sitemap url per discoverable heichel: https://awtsmoos.com/heichelos/ /sitemap.xml dynamic per heichel sitemap /heichelos/:heichel/sitemap.xml first proves the requested heichel is present in public discovery, then traverses only that heichel from series root through public series details. it emits canonical urls for: the heichel root; every discovered named series; every stable named post under its containing series. it never emits numeric road positions, api routes, submit/edit/delete pages, or private heichel identities.

searchText: b"h robots and sitemap implementation plan boruch hashem. blessed is he. the awtsmoos divides one immense map into measured vessels of oros and keilim; awtsmoos.com gains discoverability without making every crawler request rebuild every palace and every trail. new modules create heichelos/routes/heichel/sitemap/ with small files: 1. xml.js xml escaping. absolute canonical url construction. urlset and sitemapindex builders. dynamic server xml response wrapper. 2. publicheichels.js normalizes discovery response shapes. follows meta.pageinfo.nextcursor while hasmore. deduplicates valid public heichel ids. provides exact public heichel membership proof. 3. heichelgraph.js starts at series root. fetches /api/social/heichelos/:heichel/series/:series/details. normalizes child series ids and post ids from arrays or objects. uses a visited set and hard safety ceilings. returns canonical heichel/series/post paths. 4. routes.js composes the sitemap index and per heichel sitemap renderers. keeps route wiring separate from xml/data traversal. existing file rewrite rewrite heichelos/routes/heichel/createroutes.js completely after a clean file concurrency guard. add /sitemap.xml and /:heichel/sitemap.xml before the generic /:heichel route while preserving all current editor, reader, series, and shell routes. static root files create: robots.txt sitemap.xml both remain intentionally tiny and stable. safety ceilings public heichel discovery pagination: bounded loop with repeated cursor detection and maximum page count. per heichel traversal: visited series set plus maximum series count. url output: stop below sitemap protocol 50,000 url ceiling. missing/non public heichel sitemap returns an empty url set or non success response only after public membership proof; searchText: b"h sitemap discovery scaling delta boruch hashem. blessed is he. the awtsmoos revealed one hidden ceiling beneath the public discovery doorway; awtsmoos.com must not mistake a ui sized window for the whole public city when a complete map is the mission of the day. plan delta the earlier sitemap plan proposed paging /api/social/heichelos/discover. archaeology showed that heicheldiscover() truncates its no query candidate scan to the first 500 heichel ids before api pagination. paging that response therefore cannot reveal public heichelos beyond candidate 500. the canonical internals already expose a better complete path: allheicheldiscoveryids($i) gathers indexed and physical heichel ids without the ui scan cap. discoveryitem($i, heichelid, environment) applies the same publication and discoverability policy used by the public discovery endpoint. improved implementation the dynamic heichel sitemap index will use allheicheldiscoveryids() and filter each candidate through discoveryitem() with the default public environment policy. this does not duplicate privacy rules. it reuses the same canonical policy while removing only the presentation layer 500 item ceiling. a bounded batch size will prevent unbounded simultaneous database reads. ids will be deduplicated and sorted before xml rendering so the sitemap remains deterministic.
